the nonlinear 2-D thermal simulation approach is suitable for ESD and EOS thermal failure simulation in ICs.
a 1-D/2-D thermal simulator for EOS/ESD thermal failure analysis in ICs has been developed.

the development of a thermal simulator that is suitable for EOS/ESD failure modeling in IC's and that can be applied to a wide variety of IC structures.
the modeling of the transient thermal response of ICs to electrical overstress and electrostatic discharge events.
the development of an efficient thermal simulation technique for ESD/Eos thermal failure analysis in ICs.

the thermal simulation results for the power profiles of the test structures presented in the paper compare favorably with the experimental data, with an average error of 15.3 percent.
a nonlinear 2-D thermal model, which includes a detailed treatment of the heat transfer in the substrate, is necessary for accurate EOS/ESD thermal failure modeling in power MOSFETs.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to develop and implement a thermal failure model which is able to simulate the EOS/ESD failure of ICs.
a thermal simulator is developed for EOS and ESD failure analysis of ICs and the simulator is validated by comparison with the experimental data.
a thermal failure simulator for ICs has been developed and validated by comparing its results with the experimental data for the first time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the thermal failure of IC structures is a highly nonlinear function of the structural parameters, which makes it difficult to model the thermal failure using simple linear models.
the thermal failure of an IC is a complex phenomenon that cannot be described by a simple analytical expression.
a 2-D/2-D thermal failure simulation is not necessary for EOS/ESD modeling.
